content:
```for warrior tanking, with a shield you only need 2% block and + 7 defense from items to be uncrushable/uncrittable vs bosses that attack slow enough to have 100% shield block uptime.

You need 102.4% total avoidance to be uncrushable.
5/5 Anticipation puts you at 310 defense, and you need 315 for your full 5% each of Miss/Dodge/Block/Parry. That totals 20%. 

Shield Specialization (which you need 5/5 of for Improved Shield Block anyway) gives an additional 5%.

And then a lot of shields - as well as the enchant - give 2% block.

So, really all you need is 7 Def.... and a lot of shields and other equipment give 7 def.

Of particular note, Aegis of the Blood God gives exactly 2% block and 7 Defense, leaving its enchantment slot open for 7 stamina. A few other shields give either block or defense, so the other portion is intended to come from gear.```

author: Virasan
content:
“Any recommended arms talents/builds for leveling?” (UPDATED FOR 1.18*)

I see this question asked in here constantly. There is no “best” leveling build. Most people will tell you “go arms it’s the best leveling spec”. Others will say “dual wield gets really good around 40 on twow with the cc2 changes” or “I just wanna level in prot”. Honestly you can do whatever you want and you should; it’s just a game after all. Why do you want to follow a cookie cutter build anyways? All that said, a good number of people end up wanting to do so anyways.  

In an effort to address this common question, here is my recommended arms leveling talents:

Cruelty 5/5
Improved rend 2/2
Tactical mastery 3/5
Improved thunderclap 1/3
Improved charge 2/2
Tactical mastery 5/5
Improved overpower 2/2
Deep wounds 3/3
Two-handed weapon specialization 3/3
Impale 2/2
Sweeping strikes 1/1
Master strike 1/1
Master of arms 5/5
Improved slam 2/2
Improved thunderclap 2/3
Mortal strike 1/1
Unbridled wrath 5/5
Improved shouts 5/5
Enrage 5/5

Now I’m sure a bunch of people will come in and say “You should respec at 30 for sweeping strikes, or at 40 for mortal strike”. You are probably right. In fact, people can and will have endless  arguments about what order of talents is best, but most those people won’t actually sit down and write you out a list to follow like people ask, because then they have to expose themselves to the criticism of others by having an opinion. The reason I choose this order of talents is that it requires no respecing since a lot of people don’t have or want to spend the gold while leveling. It also has a few picks that won’t be optimal as a level 60 dps raiding build…. Because that’s not what it is. This is for people leveling with arms. Thunderclap may suck in a raid setting but it’s actually not terrible early on and is still a nice utility aoe you can use in addition to battle and demo shouts when your tanking in arms as a sub 60 or working on pre raid.

author: chain
content: The best example of why this is a bad idea is when you tank 4horsemen you want to taunt, not use mocking blow or challenging shout because if the chal shout or mocking blow runs out before you overtake the prior target’s threat, the horsemen is going to run across the room to whoever was previously top threat. That is because they work differently. Taunt snapshots top threat and gives you the same threat value along with a grace buffer I.e. melee need 110% of your threat to out threat you and ranged need 130% (or maybe 120% I forget) to rip threat .  Whereas chal shout and mocking blow simply put you top of threat meter for a certain period of time without copying the threat value. Once the effect of the spell ends, you have only the threat you generate with auto attacks and other spells etc.

author: Velanir
content:
**Threat Multipliers**

Threat multiplier stances (baseline):
> T_defStanceBaseline = 1.3
> T_battleStanceBaseline = 0.8

Multiplier Defiance (5/5):
> T_defiance = 1.2

Calculation for defensive stance threat with Defiance:
> T_defStance = T_defStanceBaseline * T_defiance
> T_defStance = 1.56

Calculation for Defensive Tactics multiplier:
> This is **NOT **the final threat multiplier. This multiplier will get multiplied with the base threat multiplier of battle stance in the next step. 
> **without **Defiance:
> T_defTactics = (T_defStanceBaseline - 1) * 1.8 + 1
> T_defTactics = 1,54
> **with **Defiance:
> T_defTacticsDefiance = (T_defStance - 1) * 1.8 + 1
> T_defTacticsDefiance = 2,008

Final multiplier in battle stance:
> **without **Defiance:
> T_battleStance = T_battleStanceBaseline * T_defTactics
> T_battleStance = 1,232
> **with **Defiance:
> T_battleStanceDefiance = T_battleStanceBaseline * T_defTacticsDefiance 
> T_battleStanceDefiance = 1,6064

TL/DR: Defiance is getting applied even when using battle or berserker stance with defensive tactics.
The talents do stack.
Battle/Berserker Stance + Defiance + DTactics =  1,6064
Defensive Stance + Defiance = 1.56

author: Nost
content:
These were some calcs I did a while ago to see how good BV is, as I wasn’t sure how accurate the guide was, if you see any errors lmk. 

1 SBV contributes to 1 damage, Shield Slam has a 1.5x damage to threat modifier and a base damage of 350. Shield Slam also has a 0.15 Attack power modifier. SS scales with str,crit & block value. So, to look at how much threat 1% crit , 1 strength, 1 BV provide: 

1% crit = 350 (damage at 0 ap) x 1% (chance of crit happening) x 1.5 (threat modifier on SS) x 1.2 (impale talent)= 6.4 more threat 

1% crit (at 1000ap) = 350 + 0.15 (SS AP modifier)*1000 x 1% x 1.5 x 1.2 = 9 more threat 

1 block value = 1 damage on SS x 1.5 (threat modifier) x 1.15 (toughness talent) = 1.73 extra threat. so at 5.2 block value you get 9 threat

1 strength = 2 ap x 0.15 (SS AP modifier) x 1.5 = 0.45 threat (1str also provides 0.05 bv (0.087 threat) so is actually 0.537 threat) so at 18.8 st you get 9 threat

so 1% crit provides, 18.8 st or 5.2 bv worth of threat on shield slam assuming you have 1000ap already. For reference my current gear has 930 atm.

At 0 ap 1% crit = 3.7 BV or 12 st worth of threat. So the more AP I have the more valuable crit becomes. And vice versa, the more crit I have the more valuable strength becomes.

content: It does because there's no general stat prio for furyprot other than stam > agi > str. The safe default is to approach an unknown stacked on stam and evaluate from there.

Whats important in understand Trinkets is how to use them and why, what might be true for me isnt true for you potentially

author: Guts
content:
Arp, isnt a stat worth pursuing as

A: Its a numerical Value compared to % based which your probably know from wotlk

B: It only has an effect some of the time (meaning alot of bosses get to 0 armor with common debuffs used in Classic raiding)

Then as to crit vs haste 

There's one of Warrior's most overpowered Talents called Impale which increases the damage bonus from critical strikes on skills, so crit has additional value compared to other classes (Flurry aswell in fury but we're talking arms here). Deep Wounds isnt as powerful in this Version but its still free damage (a tiny incentive for crit again).

Crit will scale with EVERYTHING you do (Strength does aswell, except execute), while haste only affects a certain percentage of your Damage. Another Reason why crit is so good for warriors is because Classic wow's system of not having crit value but instead having percentages of crit is just balanced poorly.

I could go on, but if you want to figure these things out for yourself i recommend playing around with some simming.

https://thrunk112.github.io/WarriorSim-TurtleWoW/turtle.html

--------- Easiest slam macro ----------
```
#showtooltip Slam
/startattack
/cast [noslamclip] Slam
```
Requirements tho
```
SuperWoW - modificiation
SP_SwingTimer - addon 
[SuperCleveRoidMacros](https://github.com/jrc13245/SuperCleveRoidMacros) - addon

```#showtooltip Slam
/startattack
/run if st_timer>UnitAttackSpeed"player"*0.9 then CastSpellByName("Slam") end
```
Requirements
```
SuperWoW - modificiation
SP_SwingTimer - addon 
```
Now important part u replace *0.9 with your own number

```SLAM CAST TIME / BASIC MAIN HAND WEAPON SPEED```

Your weapon swing speed can be checked via script below to account for some atack speed / haste enchants

```/script local mh, oh = UnitAttackSpeed("player"); print("MH:", mh, "OH:", oh)```

```2.45/3.45 = 0.71```
